skill.name: PDF Processing Pro
skill.description: Process PDF forms, tables, OCR, validation, and batch workflows with documented Python patterns and one included form-analysis script.
skill.summary: Guides production PDF workflows for form analysis, table extraction, OCR, validation, and batch processing.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown code fences, expected file-output examples, or CLI examples rather than hidden execution. Confirmed risk remains where OCR docs instruct sudo package installation, and semantic review found an unsanitized submission ID used in output filenames. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo commands with permission-aware setup notes and require users to confirm elevated package installation before running them.

remediation.issue: Unsanitized output filenames in batch form example
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize applicant IDs, reject path separators, and resolve output paths to ensure they remain inside the intended directory.

remediation.issue: User-controlled output paths in examples and CLI tools
remediation.suggestion: Document safe output-directory practices and warn users before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: Documented helper scripts are not all present in the scanned package
remediation.suggestion: Either include the referenced scripts or clearly label them as examples so users do not run missing or replacement scripts by mistake.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Data Used in Output Filename
semantic_findings.description: The batch form example reads applicant_id from submission data and uses it in output_file without sanitizing path separators. Untrusted IDs could create nested paths or escape the intended output directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines directly show data.get("id") feeding an output filename. It is a documentation example, so exploitability depends on user adoption, but the pattern is clear.

content.user_title: Process PDFs With Forms, Tables, and OCR
content.value_statement: Complex PDF workflows often fail when forms, tables, and scanned pages need different tools. This skill provides structured guidance and examples for reliable PDF processing.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes AcroForm fields with scripts/analyze_form.py and outputs JSON or summary data.
Documents PDF form filling, field validation, flattening, and batch-submission workflows.
Shows table extraction patterns with pdfplumber and exports to CSV, Excel, or JSON.
Explains OCR setup, image preprocessing, language selection, and text export with Tesseract.
Provides operational guidance for batch processing, logging, exit codes, and troubleshooting.
limitations: Only scripts/analyze_form.py is present; other named scripts are examples, not included files.
OCR depends on external Tesseract and Python libraries installed by the user.
Examples can write local output files and should be run in trusted project directories.
It does not verify extracted data accuracy; users must validate results.

use_cases.title: Map Form Fields Before Automation
use_cases.description: Inspect a PDF form, identify required fields, and prepare validation rules before building a fill workflow.

use_cases.title: Extract Tables From Reports
use_cases.description: Plan table extraction from multi-page reports and choose CSV, Excel, or JSON output for analysis.

use_cases.title: Add OCR to Document Pipelines
use_cases.description: Design OCR steps for scanned PDFs using preprocessing, language selection, and result validation.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Analyze One Form
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants to inspect a single PDF form.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to inspect application.pdf. List field names, field types, required fields, and any setup steps needed.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Extract Report Tables
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs structured data from a PDF report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to plan table extraction from monthly_report.pdf. Recommend detection settings, cleanup checks, and an export format.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Build an OCR Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has scanned pages with uneven image quality.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to design an OCR workflow for scanned_document.pdf. Include preprocessing, language settings, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Design Batch Processing
prompt_templates.scenario: A user must process many PDFs safely and consistently.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PDF Processing Pro to design a batch PDF pipeline for a folder of forms and reports. Include logging, validation, error handling, and output naming safeguards.

output_examples.input: A tax intake form PDF needs field discovery before automation.
output_examples.output: A field inventory grouped by type, with required fields, read-only fields, and a suggested validation plan.

output_examples.input: A scanned contract has low-quality pages.
output_examples.output: An OCR workflow with preprocessing steps, language settings, confidence checks, and a text export plan.

output_examples.input: Monthly reports contain tables across many pages.
output_examples.output: A table extraction plan comparing automatic detection, custom settings, cleanup checks, and export options.

best_practices: Validate input paths, file types, and expected PDF structure before processing.
Run examples in a dedicated working directory with backups of original documents.
Review extracted form, table, and OCR data before using it in downstream systems.
anti_patterns: Do not run package installation commands without reviewing the source and permissions.
Do not use untrusted document data directly in filenames or output paths.
Do not assume OCR or table extraction results are complete without manual checks.

faq.question: Does this skill include working scripts?
faq.answer: It includes scripts/analyze_form.py. Other scripts are documented examples and may need to be created by the user.

faq.question: Can it process scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes, the OCR guide explains Tesseract-based processing for scanned or image-based PDFs.

faq.question: Can it extract tables?
faq.answer: Yes, the table guide shows pdfplumber strategies and export patterns for CSV, Excel, and JSON.

faq.question: Is it safe to run on sensitive documents?
faq.answer: It does not show network upload behavior, but files are read and written locally. Use trusted directories and review outputs.

faq.question: What dependencies are needed?
faq.answer: The examples reference Python PDF libraries, pandas, Pillow, pytesseract, and the Tesseract OCR system package.

faq.question: Does it guarantee accurate extraction?
faq.answer: No. PDF structure, scan quality, and table layout affect results, so extracted data needs validation.
